'''Vladimir Lvovich Ashurkov''' ({{langx|ru|Владимир Львович Ашурков}}; born 15 February 1972) is a Russian political figure and the Executive Director of the [[Anti-Corruption Foundation]]. A former banker, Ashurkov was the Director of Group Portfolio Management and Control at [[Alfa Group|Alfa Group Consortium]] from 2006 to 2012, when he was asked to step down due to his political involvement with [[Alexei Navalny]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.reuters.com/article/us-russia-protest-fund-idUSBRE84U1EP20120531|title=Russian protest fund manager looks to elite for cash|date=2012-05-31|work=Reuters |accessdate=2026-02-20}}</ref> He was also on the board of the [[X5 Retail Group]] during this time.<ref>[https://www.nzz.ch/wirtschaft/der-wandel-von-londongrad-schuld-und-suehne-auf-der-britischen-buehne-ld.1295931 Schuld und Sühne auf der britischen Bühne] (''tr. "Crime and Punishment on the British Stage "'') 30 June 2017 ''nzz.ch'', accessed 13 March 2022</ref>

In 2014, a panel of the [[Investigative Committee of Russia]] accused Ashurkov of embezzling funds from Alexei Navalny's [[Alexei Navalny 2013 mayoral campaign|2013 Moscow mayoral campaign]], after which he sought and was granted political asylum in the UK, claiming the allegations were politically motivated.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.theguardian.com/world/2015/apr/01/russian-opposition-activist-is-granted-asylum-in-uk|title= Russian opposition activist Vladimir Ashurkov is granted asylum in UK |work= The Guardian|date=April 2015|author=Alec Luhn|access-date=2020-10-31}}</ref> Both Ashurkov and Navalny claim that the allegations are unfounded.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.reuters.com/article/uk-russia-navalny-idUKKBN0E310620140523|title=Russia launches fraud case against supporter of Putin critic Navalny|date=2014-05-23|work=Reuters|access-date=2017-07-15}}</ref>

After relocating, Ashurkov organised bus tours for activists and journalists, similar to [[Roman Gul]]'s "[[Kleptocracy|Kleptocrats]] Tour", "to show the opulence and corruption of the [[Russian oligarchs|Russian oligarchy]] in London." He does this, says Ashurkov, according to the [[Stuttgarter Zeitung]], to alert the British authorities to dirty money, as for example in [[Witanhurst]] owned by [[Andrey Guryev]]. Ashurkov advises the British government to dispense with the "dirty money", even though, according to Benjamin Plackett of ''[[Stuttgarter Zeitung]]'', the "intertwining of Russian wealth with the British economy" complicates the policy.<ref>{{cite news |author=Stuttgarter Zeitung, Stuttgart Germany |url=https://www.stuttgarter-zeitung.de/inhalt.superreiche-in-london-bustour-zu-den-oligarchen.d77cb6f6-5d68-4cd4-8ccb-6203e79be617.html|title=Super-rich in London: bus tour to oligarchs |publisher=[[Stuttgarter Zeitung]]|language=en |access-date=2020-10-22}}</ref>

==Early life and education==
Ashurkov was born in 1972 in Moscow<ref name = "qa">{{cite news |title=Q&A: Navalny's Fundraiser Sees the Power of the Crowd |url=https://www.themoscowtimes.com/2012/10/10/qa-navalnys-fundraiser-sees-the-power-of-the-crowd-a18502 |work=The Moscow Times |date=2012-10-10 |access-date=2026-02-20}}</ref> into a family of engineers who worked in research institutes of [[military–industrial complex]].<ref name = "newtimes">{{cite web |last=Бешлей |first=Ольга |url=http://newtimes.ru/articles/detail/53086 |title=Неутомимый оптимист |date=2012-06-03 |website=The New Times |access-date=2026-02-20 |lang=ru}}</ref> He received a Bachelor of Science degree in Physics from the Moscow Institute of Physics and Technology.<ref name = "x5">{{cite web |title=Corporate Governance Report |url=https://www.x5.ru/en/documents/reports/2011/en/corporate_governance_risk/corporate_governance_report/default.html |publisher=X5 Group |year=2011 |access-date=2026-02-20}}</ref><ref name = "bipr" />  In 1996, he graduated from the [[Wharton School of the University of Pennsylvania]] with an [[MBA]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Our Team: Vladimir Ashurkov |url=http://sloaneservices.com/ |publisher=Sloane Services |access-date=2026-02-20}}</ref><ref name = "novaya" />

==Career in business==
===Early career===
During the 1990s, Ashurkov worked as a financial analyst in PepsiCo Holding and as an investment banker in Renaissance Capital.<ref name = "qa" /> From 1999 onwards, he held executive roles in the transportation industry, including the post of financial director of the Saint Petersburg Sea Port.<ref name = "x5" />

===Alfa Group===
In 2006, he assumed the position of the Director of Group Portfolio Management at Alfa Group.<ref name = "disruption">{{cite web |title='Sanctions should be more nuanced': Vladimir Ashurkov on Russia, Ukraine, and Navalny |url=https://www.disruptionbanking.com/2023/04/30/sanctions-should-be-more-nuanced-vladimir-ashurkov-on-russia-ukraine-and-navalny/ |publisher=Disruption Banking |date=2023-04-30 |access-date=2026-02-20}}</ref> During his tenure, Ashurkov served as director of asset management at CTF Holdings, a subsidiary of Alfa Group, and as a board member of X5 Retail Group, one of Russia's largest food retail chains.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.ft.com/content/dbb50132-d890-11e4-ba53-00144feab7de |title=UK grants asylum to Russian dissident |date=2015-04-02 |website=Financial Times |first=Courtney |last=Weaver |access-date=2026-02-20}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Schedule 13D Amendment |url=https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1071321/000095012309063518/w76370sc13dza.htm |publisher=SEC.gov |date=2009-11-19 |access-date=2026-02-20}}</ref>

===Association with Alexei Navalny and departure from Alfa Group===
In 2009, Ashurkov started reading a blog of [[Alexey Navalny]], then a young lawyer who was writing about corruption, on [[LiveJournal]].<ref name = "disruption" /> As he stated in a 2012 interview to "Novaya Gazeta", Ashurkov got interested in how Navalny approaches problems, and wrote him a letter offering help on correcting some of the cases.<ref name = "novaya">{{cite web |first=Диана |last=Хачатрян |url=http://www.novayagazeta.ru/politics/52359.html |title=Владимир АШУРКОВ: «Ради чего молчать и бояться?» |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120515092140/http://www.novayagazeta.ru/politics/52359.html |date=2012-04-27 |archive-date=2012-05-15 |lang=ru |website=Новая газета}}</ref><ref name = "qa" />

As Ashurkov’s collaboration with Navalny deepened, he became his key strategic advisor.<ref name="novaya" /><ref name="slowjournalism">{{cite web |url=https://www.slow-journalism.com/long-reads/moment-that-mattered-alexei-navalny-is-arrested-after-returning-to-russia |title=Moment that mattered: Alexei Navalny is arrested upon his return to Russia |website=Delayed Gratification |date=2026-02-20}}</ref> During this period, Ashurkov was involved in managing the business of Alfa Group as the Director of Group Portfolio Management and Control, a role that involved high-level strategic analysis and oversight of major investment projects.<ref name="forbes_ru">{{cite web |first=Елена |last=Тофанюк |url=https://www.forbes.ru/sobytiya/lyudi/81639-ya-ponimal-chto-sotrudnichestvo-s-navalnym-mozhet-predstavlyat-ugrozu-dlya-moei |title=«Я понимал, что сотрудничество с Навальным может быть угрозой для моей работы» |lang=ru |website=Forbes Russia |date=2012-04-25}}</ref><ref name="moscowtimes_biz">{{cite web |url=https://www.themoscowtimes.com/2012/06/05/ashurkov-bridging-the-gap-between-business-and-politics-for-navalny-a15259 |title=Ashurkov Bridging the Gap Between Business and Politics for Navalny |website=The Moscow Times |date=2012-06-05}}</ref> In late 2010, Ashurkov informed the chairman of Alfa Group’s supervisory board, [[Mikhail Fridman]], of his work with Navalny. While Fridman remained neutral, he cautioned that Ashurkov's political leanings might likely eventually necessitate his departure from the company.<ref name="novaya" /><ref name="meduza_navalny">{{cite web |url=https://meduza.io/en/feature/2024/05/10/the-main-risk-is-that-they-ll-kill-us-all |title='The main risk is that they'll kill us all': How Navalny's team worked |website=Meduza |date=2024-05-10 |access-date=2026-02-20}}</ref> In February 2012, Fridman requested his resignation, later stating that active political engagement was "not fully tolerable" for a business of Alfa Group’s scale in the Russian context.<ref name="moscowtimes_biz" /><ref name="bfm_exit">{{cite web |url=https://www.bfm.ru/news/177393 |title=Х5 рассталась с топ-менеджером из-за политических взглядов |lang=ru |website=BFM.ru |date=2012-04-14}}</ref> Ashurkov resigned. In interviews, he stated that he had chosen civic engagement over his corporate career.<ref name="novaya" /><ref name="forbes_ru" />

==Political career==
===Foundation of ACF===
In 2012, Ashurkov became the executive director of the Anti-Corruption Foundation (FBK), which had been founded by Alexei Navalny in 2011.<ref name="bipr">{{cite web |url=https://bipr.jhu.edu/events/4714-Russian-Opposition-in-the-Time-of-War-of-Ukraine.cfm |title=Russian Opposition in the Time of War of Ukraine |website=Johns Hopkins University |date=2023-03-13}}</ref> He is credited with moving it from a volunteer-based initiative to a structured NGO with dedicated legal and economic departments.<ref name="slowjournalism" /> During the [[Alexei Navalny 2013 mayoral campaign|2013 Moscow mayoral election]], Ashurkov developed a crowdfunding mechanism for Navalny's campaign that sought to work within the constraints of Russian campaign finance regulations.<ref name="globalvoices_fundraising">{{cite web |url=https://globalvoices.org/2013/08/13/russias-soviet-assault-on-navalnys-online-fundraising/ |title=Russia's Soviet Assault on Navalny's Online Fundraising |website=Global Voices |date=2013-08-13 |access-date=2026-02-20}}</ref> 

===Political persecution and immigration from Russia===
In October 2012, Ashurkov was elected to the Russian Opposition Coordination Council, receiving 28,754 votes in the general civil list.<ref name="osw_elections">{{cite web |url=https://www.osw.waw.pl/en/publikacje/analyses/2012-10-24/russia-oppositions-coordinating-council-has-been-chosen |title=Russia: the opposition's Coordinating Council has been chosen |website=OSW |date=2012-10-24}}</ref> in May 2014, Russian authorities opened a criminal case against him, Nikolai Lyaskin, and Konstantin Yankauskas, alleging embezzlement of funds from Navalny’s mayoral campaign.<ref name="rferl_asylum">{{cite web |url=https://www.rferl.org/a/ashurkov-gets-political-asylum-in-uk/26931642.html |title=Navalny Associate Says Granted Asylum In Britain |website=Radio Free Europe/Radio Liberty |date=2015-04-01}}</ref> Ashurkov dismissed the charges as politically motivated and left Russia for the United Kingdom in 2014.<ref name="guardian_asylum">{{cite web |first=Alec |last=Luhn |url=https://www.theguardian.com/world/2015/apr/01/russian-opposition-activist-is-granted-asylum-in-uk |title=Russian opposition activist Vladimir Ashurkov is granted asylum in UK |website=The Guardian |date=2015-04-01 |access-date=2026-02-20}}</ref>

===Navalny’s arrest===
Following Alexey Navalny’s arrest in January 2021, Ashurkov published an open letter to Western leaders, including U.S. President Joe Biden, containing a "List of 35" Russian officials and oligarchs recommended for targeted sanctions.<ref name="rferl_sanctions">{{cite web |url=https://www.rferl.org/a/russia-sanctions-navalny-reaction/31131665.html |title=Kremlin Huffs, Navalny Allies Fret |website=RFE/RL |date=2021-03-03}}</ref> Ashurkov continued to assist in the FBK's international relations and strategy from London until stepping down as executive director in 2023.<ref name="bipr" />

After relocating, Ashurkov participated as a guide in kleptocracy bus tours in London, organized by the campaign group ClampK and its founder Roman Borisovich.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.globalwitness.org/en/blog/londons-newest-tourist-attraction-kleptocrats-bus-tour/ |title=London's newest tourist attraction: the kleptocrat's bus tour |website=Global Witness |date=2016}}</ref>
In 2020, Ashurkov founded Zorge Partners Limited, a London-based firm specialising in investigations, due diligence, and litigation support, with a focus on Russia and Eastern Europe.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://zorgepartners.com/about |title=About Us |website=Zorge Partners}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Ashurkov is married to Alexandrina Markvo, a theatrical producer and the founder of the arts production company Bird & Carrot.<ref name="guardian_asylum" /><ref name="birdandcarrot">{{cite web |url=https://birdandcarrot.com/#about |title=About Bird&Carrot |website=birdandcarrot.com}}</ref> Markvo also sought and received asylum in the UK after being targeted by a fraud investigation in Russia that was regarded as politically motivated due to her husband's activism.<ref name="hjs_markvo">{{cite web |url=https://henryjacksonsociety.org/media-centre/uk-must-oppose-russias-persecution-of-wife-of-prominent-putin-critic-say-hjs-experts/ |title=UK must oppose Russia's persecution of wife of prominent Putin critic |website=Henry Jackson Society |date=2015-03-19 |accessdate=2026-02-20}}</ref> The couple resides in London with their two sons, Nikola and Lev, and Markvo's daughter from a previous marriage, Ariadna.<ref name="guardian_asylum" /><ref name="independent_asylum">{{cite web |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/news/world/europe/russian-dissident-vladimir-ashurkov-seeks-asylum-in-britain-9778476.html |title=Russian dissident Vladimir Ashurkov seeks asylum in Britain |website=The Independent |date=2014-10-06 |access-date=2026-02-20}}</ref>
